top_needs.title: Practice efficiency gains and ROI with DM-monitored braces and aligners versus standard recall
top_needs.brands_and_products: Damon, ormco, KLOwen, Lightforce, Spark, Angel, suresmile, Invisalign, clearcorrect, SmartSTL, self-ligating braces, Twin brackets, damon ultima brackets, SLB, Aliwell
top_needs.metrics_sought: chair time reduction, appointment frequency, ROI, profitability, time saving, visit reduction, ongoing monitoring costs vs benefits, staff efficiency, practice optimisation, rentability, diary changes, adaptive aligner change, average visit reduction, efficiency in second and third order movements, decrease of emergencies, dynamic scheduling
top_needs.doctor_objections: Doctors question whether DM actually saves time or money, reduces appointments, or improves practice profitability. Some are skeptical that workflow changes will translate into real efficiency or financial gains, especially for braces. Others doubt that staff will benefit or that the investment is justified.
top_needs.evidence_type_needed: academic publication, case study, peer-reviewed, white paper, No format preference specified — reps asked for any available evidence
sample_queries: How much chair time reduction achieved
How can I make DM work in a practice with 8 chairs and 15 assistants in a way that they really get the real benefits and make it work financially as well in The Netherlands?
Could you provide any data demonstrating improved patient compliance with DM or its impact on patient outcomes
reduced chairtime, savings and only Australian studies
Show how can doctors increases the profitability if their practices using DM
top_needs.gap_assessment: Direct, high-quality comparative studies quantifying ROI and efficiency for both aligners and braces, especially in diverse geographies and practice sizes, are limited. More robust, region-specific economic analyses and workflow impact studies should be prioritized.

top_needs.title: Accuracy and reliability of DM’s AI and SmartSTL for clinical monitoring and diagnostics
top_needs.metrics_sought: AI accuracy, specificity and sensitivity, reliability, accuracy of SmartSTL, comparison to intraoral scan, FDA class I, occlusal assessment, accuracy of AI detecting malocclusions, accuracy of scanning, AI vs orthodontist
top_needs.doctor_objections: Doctors express skepticism about whether DM’s AI is accurate enough for clinical decision-making, especially for detecting clinical observations or malocclusions. Some fear AI may miss issues or not match human expertise, and others specifically distrust SmartSTL’s reliability.
top_needs.evidence_type_needed: academic publication, white paper, peer-reviewed, No format preference specified — reps asked for any available evidence
sample_queries: Information on the accuracy of DM, a patient has questioned the ability of the AI to detect clinical observations
Specificity and sensitivity results for FDA application
How accurate is SmartSTL AI
Looking for white papers on Smart STL accuracy to help convince a doctor to use it in the practice.

Occlusal Assessment: A quantitative study validating the AI’s accuracy in detecting malocclusions (midline deviation, overbite, overjet, and canine relationship) found that the mean bias across all parameters was less than 0.5 mm, confirming its reliability as a remote diagnosis and triage tool.
top_needs.gap_assessment: There is a need for more peer-reviewed, head-to-head studies comparing DM’s AI and SmartSTL to human clinicians and other digital tools, especially for specific diagnostic tasks and in real-world clinical settings.
